📚 CBDCs vs Stablecoins

• A CBDC is a direct liability of a central bank; a stablecoin is a liability of a private issuer backed by reserves.

• CBDC designs vary by country between retail (public-facing) and wholesale (interbank-only) models.

• Policy debates around CBDCs often center on privacy, financial stability and the role of commercial banks.
